title: Seahawks sign Terrion Arnold; NFL to place CB on commissioner’s exempt list
content:
Terrion Arnold finally signed his contract with the Seattle Seahawks on Saturday, according to the team, but it remains unclear when he’ll actually suit up for the franchise.

An NFL spokesman told The Athletic that Arnold will be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list while he faces kidnapping and armed robbery charges in Tampa, Fla. His placement on that list will prevent him from practicing or playing while the league investigates and considers potential punishment under the personal conduct policy, but he will be paid and can attend team meetings.

On Aug. 14, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team had an agreement in place to sign Arnold, but the transaction did not happen until after Friday night’s preseason finale. Both sides honored the agreement, which allows Arnold to join the team despite his NFL future being up in the air.

“It was an opportunity to bring on a player that we felt strongly about during the draft process,” Macdonald said of bringing in Arnold two weeks ago. “We also understand that it’s a serious situation with a legal matter. There’s a process behind it, so we respect that. That’s how we’ll operate, just letting that process play out and let the league decide if and when his return to play is.”

The Detroit Lions released Arnold, their first-round pick out of Alabama in 2024, less than a week after he was arrested in June on kidnapping and armed robbery charges stemming from a February incident in Tampa. He is due to appear in person in court on Oct. 5.

In two seasons with the Lions, he played in 24 games and recorded one interception. A shoulder injury ended his 2025 season after eight games.

“We think his skill set fits in our secondary,” Macdonald said two weeks ago. “He plays with a lot of energy, physicality. Some of the pattern-match stuff is more up his alley that he did at Alabama. Then, personality-wise, there’s an opportunity there if he’s the best version of himself that he can be a fit for us.”

Seattle has dealt with a rash of injuries to its secondary throughout training camp. The team placed safety Bud Clark on injured reserve Tuesday, and he will miss the 2026 season. Second-year nickelback Nick Emmanwori has not practiced with the team since having offseason ankle surgery.

On Thursday, Macdonald declined to answer a question about how many practices Emmanwori will need to be ready for their season opener Sept. 9 — a Super Bowl rematch against the New England Patriots.

Given Seattle’s lack of defensive back depth, the team signed former Dallas Cowboys cornerback Trevon Diggs on Aug. 19. Diggs, who turns 28 in September, did not record an interception last season for the first time in his six-year NFL career.

He played eight games with the Cowboys in 2025 before being waived, and played two more for the Green Bay Packers (including playoffs) before they released him.

Diggs and Arnold join a secondary headlined by cornerback Devon Witherspoon, who agreed to a four-year, $132 million extension on Aug. 15. Cornerback Josh Jobe signed a three-year deal in March as well after starting a career-high 15 games.

Diggs could be the front-runner to be the Seahawks’ third cornerback and replace Riq Woolen, who signed with the Philadelphia Eagles in free agency. He strengthened his case in Seattle’s preseason finale, intercepting Garrett Nussmeier. It is unclear, meanwhile, what Arnold’s role will be once he is permitted to play this season, if at all.

“You see the movement skills, you see the physicality, and that’s the stuff that we saw coming out of school,” Macdonald said two weeks ago. “That’s what made us think that he could be a good fit in our defense.”
